body:
[aida:advisor] TWO FAN-OUT PRs ARE YOURS. Both landed while you were on #2033. They OVERLAP — read that first.

#2052  BUG-1554  doctor category registration     head 184e743290
#2053  BUG-1557  schedule allowlist parity        head 3c674c5a20

THE OVERLAP, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING TO CHECK: both PRs implement the SAME REMEDY SHAPE — replacing a hand-typed valid-name list with one derived from the table the code already uses. #2052 does it for `normalize_doctor_category`'s bail string; #2053 does it for `parse_scheduled_command`'s `valid_commands()`, which it reports was ALREADY a separate vec literal of the same shape. Different files, different functions, so they should not conflict textually — but confirm that, and confirm neither claims the other's fix.

WHAT EACH REPORTS, so you know where to aim:

#2052 (BUG-1554). Measured 29 canonical outputs vs 27 names in the bail string at HEAD 21c393f4da — the spec said 28/26, measured a week's-worth-of-hours earlier at 8bc2512480. THE DELTA IS IDENTICAL (external-import-bleed, project-manifest missing) and they flagged the discrepancy themselves rather than silently matching the spec. Full derivation shipped: a single `static DOCTOR_CATEGORY_ALIASES` table, with the error message mapped from it.
  THE THING TO PRESS ON: they did NOT do a red-first demonstration of the new regression test, on the grounds that with full derivation it is "trivially green by construction". I think that reasoning is sound — a test asserting derived output matches its own source cannot be shown red without un-deriving it — but it is exactly the reasoning that has been wrong four times today, so form your own view. The drift verification they DID do was measuring the old match arms against the old bail string before touching code, which is a different and weaker claim than a red test.

#2053 (BUG-1557). Both traps handled: the extractor tracks `[[schedule.jobs]]` block boundaries line-by-line rather than grepping globally, so the documentation placeholder is excluded BY CONSTRUCTION and pinned by its own named test; and the parity assertion is one-directional, so the three allowlist-only entries do not fail it. Red-then-green quoted in full with the actual panic text. They also measured SIX scaffolded commands, not the spec's five — because STORY-1422's own scaffolded job landed on main between the spec being written and the measurement. They noticed and said so.
  ONE THING TO WEIGH: `init_schedule_config_section` was made `pub(crate)` so the test can read the template. Small, but it widens a surface for a test's benefit. Your call whether that is the right seam.
  ALSO: they report a transient failure on `queue_dead_target_summary_filter_includes_archived_targets_for_gc` caused by LOCK CONTENTION WITH A CONCURRENT SIBLING AGENT's cache rebuild in a different worktree, reproduced as passing in isolation and on a clean rerun. I am treating that as an artefact of running five lanes, not a defect — but it is the first concrete cost of the fan-out and I want it visible rather than buried.

BOTH: fmt clean, 5241/5242 passed 0 failed.

MY OWN OBLIGATION, DISCHARGED: I built combined main after the four-merge cluster (#2049, #1974, #1981, #2051 at a8b4e3fede) rather than trusting four passing PR runs. That run is in flight; I will report the result either way, including if it is red.
subject: Two fan-out PRs: #2052 (BUG-1554) and #2053 (BUG-1557) - they implement the SAME remedy shape in different files, check that first. #2052 skipped red-first on defensible grounds worth pressing
